va_romeo_s_ladder.blurb: Romeo's Ladder is one of the busier cliffs along the Potomac gorge at Great Falls, sitting between the Seclusion and Aid Box sections. Most of its fifteen climbs are trad lines that double as top-rope laps, with a single boulder problem and one easy scramble thrown in. Grades run from beginner-level up to hard 5.12, though the bulk sit between 5.9 and 5.12, with a few easier crack and chimney lines to start on. Trees serve as anchors for top-roping from the clifftop, and the setting is sunny and often crowded with other climbers and hikers. Water level in the river can swallow the belay ledges, so check conditions first.

va_thunderbolt_boulder.blurb: Thunderbolt Boulder is a single block in the Gasland pocket of Upper Darkside, in the Guest River Gorge bouldering. It has an unusual shape: a very low roof on one flank, an easy slab across the front, and taller vertical faces on the other side, plus a nice arete along the nose. Fifteen problems are logged, from VB up to V8, with the biggest cluster around V3. That makes it workable for a mixed group, with a few warm-ups and a handful of hard lines. It lies within sight of the neighboring Pegasus Boulder, a bit further on through open forest.

va_cascadia.blurb: Cascadia is a big sandstone boulder beside the creek in the Cascades recreation area near Blacksburg, a short stroll from the parking lot. The front is a steep roof, and the sides hold shorter vertical problems. Fifteen problems are logged across a wide spread: a couple of very easy ones, a middle band from V2 to V6, and a few serious lines in the V7 to V9 range, so it suits both a casual session and a project day. Other boulders are scattered nearby along the same trail, making it an easy part of a longer bouldering outing.

va_picnic_boulder.blurb: Picnic Boulder is a short but long, steep block in Grayson Highlands State Park, tucked into the rhododendrons just across the road from the large Olympus Boulder. The downhill end carries a big overhanging roof with a pale band running through its middle. Fifteen problems are logged: a good batch of V1s, a few V2 and V3 lines, and a harder group around V6, with one V5 between. Because it sits away from the busier Rock House and Olympus boulders, it tends to be a quieter place to spend a session, and the steepness rewards strong, powerful climbing.

va_cornice.blurb: Cornice is a roughly 50-foot cliff in the Great Falls gorge on the Potomac, a little downstream of Bird's Nest. Its headline line follows a corner into a chimney and out through a big roof, and is often called the best moderate climb in the gorge. Of the fifteen routes, most are trad leads that also work on top-rope, plus one scramble. Grades run from easy up to 5.11, with a strong cluster at 5.10 and a few mid-range lines around 5.7. The cliff top is only a few yards from the river trail, so setting top-ropes is simple. Poison ivy grows at the base.
